task1ToolShapeDecision.decision: LIST-THEN-READ PAIR, not one combined tool.
reasoning: Matches the established codebase convention already used twice in this same file: find_parcel -> get_smart_site, and list_screens (summary) -> screen rows. A third pattern-breaking shape (one giant combined tool) would be the odd one out.

Size: extractedText is full OCR text of a courthouse recording (can be many KB per document). A parcel can have multiple records-request jobs, each with multiple artifacts. Returning full extractedText for every document on every job in one call risks the same response-size problem tools.ts already documents and works around elsewhere (H2 comment on SMARTSITE_NODE_BATCH_CAP: the host writes results over ~150,000 chars to a file and hands the panel a pointer instead of showing it, measured 2026-08-30). A list call stays small (state + metadata only, no body text); a read call returns exactly one document's full text, bounded by construction.

Matches the dispatch's given data shape directly: 'learn what documents exist' (list) is a materially different question from 'read what was extracted from each' (read), and the caller (an LLM agent) benefits from seeing the list first to choose which document is worth a full read, exactly the find_parcel -> get_smart_site flow.

threeStateRequirement.rule: pending, failed (with failureReason), and complete-with-text must never collapse to one bit.
threeStateRequirement.implementation: readState field, FOUR literal values (not three): pending | complete | failed | skipped. The underlying stored type (VisionReadStatus in recordsRequestArtifactVision.ts) is itself 'complete' | 'failed' | 'skipped' (skipped = vision_client_unavailable, a system-level non-attempt; failed = an attempt was made and produced no usable text, e.g. blank_capture or vision_read_produced_no_text). Collapsing skipped into failed would itself violate the absent/zero/unmeasured-are-different-states rule (ENFORCEMENT.md) by hiding WHY no text exists. pending is added as the fourth value for the case metadata.visionRead is not present at all (vision read has not run on this artifact yet) -- this is the state absent from the stored type entirely and had to be introduced by this lane's read path, not invented data. failureReason travels alongside failed and skipped verbatim from stored metadata; extractedText travels only alongside complete.
threeStateRequirement.classifyStateSameTreatment: classifyState field, four literal values: pending | written | refused | skipped, mirroring ArtifactClassifyStatus ('written'|'refused'|'skipped') plus pending for metadata.classify absent.

purchaseCostPlacement.decision: SAME response, both tools, not a separate call.
purchaseCostPlacement.reasoning: acquisitionMethod and purchaseCostCents are columns on the exact same records_request_artifacts row already being read for vision/classify state -- there is no second query, no second round trip, and no additional DB load to include them. list_purchased_records also surfaces the job-level runCost (jsonb on records_request_jobs) once per job. Splitting this into a separate call would add latency and a second auth/gate check for data that costs nothing extra to include now.
